findings.sourceEvidence:
"(n)
Dispositions of Property from any Subsidiary that is not a Loan Party to any other Subsidiary that is not a Loan Party."
findings.verifierReasoning: The operative boundary of carve-out (n) is that the transferor must be a Subsidiary that is not a Loan Party and the transferee must be another (i.e., a different) Subsidiary that is not a Loan Party. The only limitation the proposed IR encodes is a negative scope: entities that are Loan Parties are excluded. Because both the entityScope include list and the conditions array are empty for r1, and capacity is UNLIMITED, the rule as encoded reads as an unlimited permission for any non-Loan-Party entity to dispose Property to any non-Loan-Party entity. That is broader than the source, which restricts the exception to dispositions between Subsidiaries of the Parent Borrower. Concretely, a disposition by a non-Loan-Party Subsidiary to an unrelated non-Loan-Party entity that is not a Subsidiary (e.g., a joint venture that is not a Subsidiary) would satisfy the encoded rule but does not qualify for exception (n) under the source text, which only covers transfers to 'any other Subsidiary'. The 'other' (distinctness) requirement is also dropped. A competent reviewer relying on the IR could reach a different conclusion about whether a given disposition is permitted under (n). Note this is a positive scope assertion, not merely an unspecified gap, so it is a genuine misstatement of the exception's boundary.

findings.sourceEvidence: "Any Collateral which is sold, transferred or otherwise conveyed pursuant to this Section 7.5 to a Person other than the Parent Borrower and its Subsidiaries shall, upon the consummation of such sale ... be released from the Liens..."
findings.verifierReasoning: The release condition in the source requires that the collateral be conveyed 'to a Person other than the Parent Borrower and its Subsidiaries' - i.e., the transferee must be outside the Parent Borrower's group. The machine-readable expression the IR builds for this condition compares an empty entity-scope reference for equality with the single term 'Person'; it does not encode the operative exclusion of 'the Parent Borrower and its Subsidiaries' anywhere in the expression. Taken literally, the expression would read as 'scope equals any Person', which loses the exclusion that is the entire point of the condition (the release is not triggered for dispositions to group entities). The accompanying human-readable description does state the correct meaning and the condition is flagged UNSUPPORTED/requiredReview, so a reviewer is warned; but the structured form itself mis-encodes the triggering boundary, meaning downstream automated use of this condition could produce a different (broader) conclusion about when the release applies. I mark this UNCERTAIN because the accurate description and the explicit UNSUPPORTED flag mitigate the practical impact, but the encoded boundary does not match the source.
